lines.say: Why does one of these terrifying night creatures act
almost like a friend?
This is The Sleep of Reason Produces Monsters,
engraved by Francisco Goya in 1799.
A man sleeps at his desk
while owls and a lynx crowd in behind him.
But look at the owl.
It holds a stylus out to him.
The owl doesn't bite. The owl doesn't scream.
The owl simply offers.
According to Goya's own caption,
fantasy abandoned by reason produced impossible monsters.
Monsters should come to destroy the dreamer.
But united with reason,
fantasy was the mother of arts.
And here's the disturbing part.
The creatures surround a sleeping man,
yet one hands him his tool.
As if the nightmare wants him to keep drawing.
So what is the owl asking him to draw?
